If H and L are used to describe dissyllables in Tangwang, we can say that generally the H accent is on the syllable [sic: word missing in the Google Books text layer]. In Chinese morphology, the suffix tsy is added to a word to form a noun. In Standard Mandarin, this suffix is atonal; in other words, the accent is on the first tonal syllable. new_statements.rule_in_words: Among Hui (Muslim) speakers, lexical tone is lost on monosyllables and disyllabic words carry a Low-High accent pattern, i.e. prominence (H accent/stress) on the final syllable, even on the nominal suffix -tsɿ that is toneless/unstressed in Standard Mandarin; the pattern matches stress-final Dongxiang. Han speakers in Tangwang keep a reduced (2-3) tone system and do not necessarily stress the suffix.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing seen in the accessible snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: 'general tendency is LH and not the reverse' (so not exceptionless); Han speakers pattern more like Standard Mandarin (suffix -tsɿ not necessarily stressed); speakers told the author context, not stress, disambiguates disyllabic homophones (p.74); one Han informant uses three tones (fn.31).
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern disyllabic words in citation/reading forms and a perception test of disyllabic homophones (Tables 3.11-3.13); described as an H/L 'accent' opposition replacing tone rather than classic dynamic stress. Access was via page-numbered Google Books snippets; one snippet sentence reads 'generally the H accent is on the syllable' with a word apparently missing in the printed text, so the LH/final reading rests on pp. 70 and 76.
new_statements.identity_note: Xu 2017 describes the speech of Tangwang town (唐汪川), Dongxiang Autonomous County, Linxia Hui Prefecture, Gansu = Glottolog tang1373. The stress-final/LH statement applies specifically to Hui (Muslim, incl. converted Tang/Wang clans) speakers; Han speakers in the same villages are described as retaining a reduced 2-3-tone system closer to Hezhou/Linxia Mandarin. Djamouri (2022, 2025) treats the same variety as having three low-amplitude contrastive tones and regards the tone-vs-accent question as unresolved.
